1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import argparse
4	import json
5	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
6	from pathlib import Path
7	from typing import Sequence
8	
9	import holidays
10	import lightgbm as lgb
11	import matplotlib.dates as mdates
12	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
13	import numpy as np
14	import pandas as pd  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
15	from matplotlib.axes import Axes
16	from matplotlib.figure import Figure
17	from numpy.typing import NDArray
18	
19	TIMESTAMP_COLUMN = "utc_timestamp"
20	LOAD_COLUMN = "DE_load_actual_entsoe_transparency"
21	TARGET_START = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
22	TARGET_END = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-08 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
23	TARGET_HOURS = 168
24	TRAINING_YEARS = 2
25	BACKTEST_YEARS = (2017, 2018, 2019)
26	RANDOM_SEED = 42
27	REFERENCE_TIME = pd.Timestamp("2015-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
28	
29	ACTUAL_COLOR = "#2a78d6"
30	FORECAST_COLOR = "#eb6834"
31	SURFACE_COLOR = "#fcfcfb"
32	TEXT_COLOR = "#0b0b0b"
33	SECONDARY_TEXT_COLOR = "#52514e"
34	MUTED_COLOR = "#898781"
35	GRID_COLOR = "#e1e0d9"
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class ModelRun:
40	    training_start: pd.Timestamp
41	    training_end: pd.Timestamp
42	    forecast: pd.Series
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class BacktestReport:
47	    year: int
48	    training_start_utc: str
49	    training_end_utc: str
50	    metrics: dict[str, float]
51	
52	
53	def make_target_index() -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
54	    return pd.date_range(TARGET_START, TARGET_END, freq="h", inclusive="left")
55	
56	
57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load
78	
79	
80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")
95	
96	
97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual
108	
109	
110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features
144	
145	
146	def build_model() -> lgb.LGBMRegressor:
147	    return lgb.LGBMRegressor(
148	        objective="regression_l2",
149	        n_estimators=400,
150	        learning_rate=0.04,
151	        num_leaves=16,
152	        max_depth=6,
153	        min_child_samples=50,
154	        subsample=0.9,
155	        subsample_freq=1,
156	        colsample_bytree=0.9,
157	        reg_lambda=1.0,
158	        random_state=RANDOM_SEED,
159	        n_jobs=-1,
160	        verbosity=-1,
161	    )
162	
163	
164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,
186	    )
187	
188	
189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }
217	
218	
219	def run_backtests(load: pd.Series) -> list[BacktestReport]:
220	    reports: list[BacktestReport] = []
221	    for year in BACKTEST_YEARS:
222	        start = pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
223	        forecast_index = pd.date_range(start, periods=TARGET_HOURS, freq="h")
224	        if forecast_index[-1] not in load.index:
225	            continue
226	
227	        run = fit_and_forecast(load, forecast_index)
228	        actual = load.loc[forecast_index]
229	        reports.append(
230	            BacktestReport(
231	                year=year,
232	                training_start_utc=run.training_start.isoformat(),
233	                training_end_utc=run.training_end.isoformat(),
234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports
238	
239	
240	def average_backtest_metrics(backtests: list[BacktestReport]) -> dict[str, float]:
241	    if not backtests:
242	        return {}
243	
244	    metric_names = tuple(backtests[0].metrics)
245	    return {
246	        name: float(np.mean([report.metrics[name] for report in backtests]))
247	        for name in metric_names
248	    }
249	
250	
251	def build_forecast_table(actual: pd.Series, forecast: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
252	    table = pd.DataFrame(
253	        {
254	            "actual_load_mw": actual,
255	            "forecast_load_mw": forecast,
256	        }
257	    )
258	    table["error_mw"] = table["forecast_load_mw"] - table["actual_load_mw"]
259	    table["absolute_percentage_error"] = (
260	        table["error_mw"].abs() / table["actual_load_mw"].abs() * 100.0
261	    )
262	    table.index.name = TIMESTAMP_COLUMN
263	    return table
264	
265	
266	def add_endpoint_label(
267	    axes: Axes,
268	    timestamp: pd.Timestamp,
269	    value: float,
270	    label: str,
271	    color: str,
272	    y_offset: int,
273	) -> None:
274	    axes.scatter(
275	        [timestamp],
276	        [value],
277	        s=42,
278	        color=color,
279	        edgecolor=SURFACE_COLOR,
280	        linewidth=2,
281	        zorder=4,
282	    )
283	    axes.annotate(
284	        label,
285	        xy=(timestamp, value),
286	        xytext=(12, y_offset),
287	        textcoords="offset points",
288	        color=TEXT_COLOR,
289	        fontsize=8.5,
290	        va="center",
291	        arrowprops={"arrowstyle": "-", "color": color, "linewidth": 1.0},
292	    )
293	
294	
295	def plot_forecast(
296	    table: pd.DataFrame,
297	    metrics: dict[str, float],
298	    output_path: Path,
299	) -> None:
300	    figure: Figure
301	    axes: Axes
302	    figure, axes = plt.subplots(figsize=(13, 6.5), constrained_layout=True)
303	    figure.patch.set_facecolor(SURFACE_COLOR)
304	    axes.set_facecolor(SURFACE_COLOR)
305	
306	    axes.plot(
307	        table.index,
308	        table["actual_load_mw"],
309	        color=ACTUAL_COLOR,
310	        linewidth=2.0,
311	        solid_capstyle="round",
312	        label="Actual load",
313	    )
314	    axes.plot(
315	        table.index,
316	        table["forecast_load_mw"],
317	        color=FORECAST_COLOR,
318	        linewidth=2.0,
319	        solid_capstyle="round",
320	        label="Forecast",
321	    )
322	
323	    axes.set_title(
324	        "German hourly electricity load: actual vs forecast",
325	        loc="left",
326	        color=TEXT_COLOR,
327	        fontsize=16,
328	        fontweight="semibold",
329	        pad=24,
330	    )
331	    axes.text(
332	        0.0,
333	        1.015,
334	        (
335	            "1 to 7 January 2020, UTC  |  "
336	            f"MAE {metrics['mae_mw']:,.0f} MW  |  "
337	            f"MAPE {metrics['mape_percent']:.2f}%  |  "
338	            f"R² {metrics['r_squared']:.3f}"
339	        ),

341	        color=SECONDARY_TEXT_COLOR,
342	        fontsize=9.5,

344	    )
345	    axes.set_ylabel("Load (MW)", color=SECONDARY_TEXT_COLOR)
346	    axes.set_xlabel("Timestamp (UTC)", color=SECONDARY_TEXT_COLOR, labelpad=12)
347	    axes.yaxis.set_major_formatter(lambda value, _: f"{value:,.0f}")
348	    axes.xaxis.set_major_locator(mdates.DayLocator(tz=mdates.UTC))  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
349	    axes.xaxis.set_major_formatter(
350	        mdates.DateFormatter("%b %d", tz=mdates.UTC)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]
351	    )
352	    axes.grid(axis="y", color=GRID_COLOR, linewidth=0.8)
353	    axes.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
354	    axes.tick_params(colors=MUTED_COLOR, labelsize=9)
355	    axes.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
356	    axes.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
357	    axes.spines["left"].set_color(GRID_COLOR)
358	    axes.spines["bottom"].set_color(GRID_COLOR)
359

361	        loc="upper left",
362	        frameon=False,
363	        ncols=2,
364	        bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.99),

366	    )
367	    for text in legend.get_texts():
368	        text.set_color(TEXT_COLOR)
369	
370	    final_timestamp = table.index[-1]
371	    final_actual = float(table["actual_load_mw"].iloc[-1])
372	    final_forecast = float(table["forecast_load_mw"].iloc[-1])
373	    if final_actual >= final_forecast:
374	        actual_offset, forecast_offset = 10, -14
375	    else:
376	        actual_offset, forecast_offset = -14, 10
377	    add_endpoint_label(
378	        axes,
379	        final_timestamp,

384	    )
385	    add_endpoint_label(

387	        final_timestamp,

393	    axes.set_xlim(table.index[0], table.index[-1] + pd.Timedelta(hours=12))
394	
395	    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
396	    figure.savefig(output_path, dpi=180, facecolor=figure.get_facecolor())
397	    plt.close(figure)
398	
399	
400	def write_metrics_report(
401	    path: Path,
402	    run: ModelRun,

1	# Personal preferences (Dermot)
2	
3	These apply across every project. Project-level `CLAUDE.md` files can
4	override or extend them. The Codex review workflow, planning rules, and
5	discipline rules live in `~/.claude/rules/workflows.md` — do not duplicate.
6	
7	## Communication
8	
9	- Be direct. Skip preamble like "Great question!", "Sure, I can help with
10	  that!", "Let me…". Just answer.
11	- No sycophancy. Do not flatter the question or the work. If something is
12	  wrong, say so. If something is fine, say so plainly.
13	- State uncertainty honestly. Prefer "I am not sure, here is how I would
14	  check" over a confident-sounding guess. If you genuinely do not know,
15	  say "I do not know" rather than assembling a plausible-sounding answer.
16	- Match response length to the task. A one-line question gets a one-line
17	  answer. A design question gets a design answer. No padding.
18	- For exploratory questions ("how should we approach X?"), answer in 2–3
19	  sentences with a recommendation and the main tradeoff. Treat it as a
20	  starting point I can redirect, not a decided plan.
21	- Never use em-dashes in prose, whether in chat replies or in written
22	  artefacts (papers, docs, commit messages). They read as an AI tell; humans
23	  rarely reach for them. Use commas, parentheses, a colon, a semicolon, or a
24	  separate sentence instead. Plain hyphens and en-dashes for number ranges
25	  (e.g. 2021 to 2024) are fine; the ban is specifically the em-dash and, in
26	  LaTeX, the `---` form. After writing or editing any prose, grep the text I
27	  added for em-dashes before finalising.
28	
29	## Explanation style
30	
31	- Default to Feynman-style: plain language first, jargon only when it pulls
32	  weight. The audience is a smart professional in an adjacent field, not a
33	  layperson and not a specialist in this exact niche.
34	- Show the mental model, not just the procedure. "Here is what is actually
35	  happening, then here is the command" beats "run this command".
36	- For formal academic writing, use the `feynman-academic` skill. For plain-
37	  language explanation aimed at non-technical professionals, use
38	  `feynman-explainer`. Both are global skills; invoke them by name.
39	
40	## Code style — Python (default language)
41	
42	- Type hints on every function signature and on non-trivial locals. Use
43	  `from __future__ import annotations` to keep forward references cheap.
44	- Prefer dataclasses or `pydantic.BaseModel` over loose dicts when the
45	  shape is fixed.
46	- Standard formatters: `ruff format`, `ruff check --fix`, `mypy --strict`.
47	  If a project has its own config, follow that instead.
48	- Tests: pytest. Write the failing test first when adding behaviour.
49	  Outside-in (start from the consumer) — see `workflows.md`.
50	
51	## Code style — general
52	
53	- Three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction.
54	- Read existing code before modifying it. Match local conventions over my
55	  global preferences.
56	- No comments for what the code does. Comments only for *why* something
57	  non-obvious is the way it is.
58	- No backwards-compatibility shims, no `_unused` placeholders, no "removed
59	  X" comments. Just delete cleanly.
60	
61	## Verification
62	
63	- For any claim about config, settings, installed state, or what a flag
64	  does: read the actual file or run the verification command before
65	  asserting. The `debug-config` skill exists for exactly this; use it.
66	- If I push back on a config claim, do not re-explain — re-read ground
67	  truth.
68	
69	## Tools and surfaces I care about
70	
71	- I am on a Claude Max subscription. The interactive CLI and `claude -p`
72	  bill against the plan. The Agent SDK does not (yet) — it bills API rates

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load

80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features

147	    return lgb.LGBMRegressor(
148	        objective="regression_l2",
149	        n_estimators=400,
150	        learning_rate=0.04,
151	        num_leaves=16,

153	        min_child_samples=50,

164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,
186	    )

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

219	def run_backtests(load: pd.Series) -> list[BacktestReport]:
220	    reports: list[BacktestReport] = []
221	    for year in BACKTEST_YEARS:
222	        start = pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
223	        forecast_index = pd.date_range(start, periods=TARGET_HOURS, freq="h")
224	        if forecast_index[-1] not in load.index:
225	            continue
226	
227	        run = fit_and_forecast(load, forecast_index)
228	        actual = load.loc[forecast_index]
229	        reports.append(
230	            BacktestReport(
231	                year=year,
232	                training_start_utc=run.training_start.isoformat(),
233	                training_end_utc=run.training_end.isoformat(),
234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports

240	def average_backtest_metrics(backtests: list[BacktestReport]) -> dict[str, float]:
241	    if not backtests:
242	        return {}
243	
244	    metric_names = tuple(backtests[0].metrics)
245	    return {
246	        name: float(np.mean([report.metrics[name] for report in backtests]))
247	        for name in metric_names
248	    }

478	def main() -> int:
479	    args = parse_args()
480	    load = load_hourly_load(args.data)
481	    _, actual = split_training_and_target(load)

58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}

62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")

65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:

70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),

80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:

83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features

164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports

1	# Notes for the AI
2	
3	Python project. The file `opsd_de_load.csv` in this directory has hourly

1	from __future__ import annotations

53	def make_target_index() -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
54	    return pd.date_range(TARGET_START, TARGET_END, freq="h", inclusive="left")

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load
78	
79	
80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")
95

97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features

164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,
186	    )

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load

80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features

164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,
186	    )

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:
173	        raise ValueError("At least one year of hourly training observations is required.")
174	
175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,
186	    )
187	
188	
189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }
217	
218	
219	def run_backtests(load: pd.Series) -> list[BacktestReport]:
220	    reports: list[BacktestReport] = []
221	    for year in BACKTEST_YEARS:
222	        start = pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
223	        forecast_index = pd.date_range(start, periods=TARGET_HOURS, freq="h")
224	        if forecast_index[-1] not in load.index:
225	            continue
226	
227	        run = fit_and_forecast(load, forecast_index)
228	        actual = load.loc[forecast_index]
229	        reports.append(
230	            BacktestReport(
231	                year=year,
232	                training_start_utc=run.training_start.isoformat(),
233	                training_end_utc=run.training_end.isoformat(),
234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports
238	
239	
240	def average_backtest_metrics(backtests: list[BacktestReport]) -> dict[str, float]:
241	    if not backtests:
242	        return {}
243	
244	    metric_names = tuple(backtests[0].metrics)
245	    return {
246	        name: float(np.mean([report.metrics[name] for report in backtests]))
247	        for name in metric_names
248	    }
249

251	def build_forecast_table(actual: pd.Series, forecast: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
252	    table = pd.DataFrame(
253	        {
254	            "actual_load_mw": actual,
255	            "forecast_load_mw": forecast,
256	        }
257	    )
258	    table["error_mw"] = table["forecast_load_mw"] - table["actual_load_mw"]
259	    table["absolute_percentage_error"] = (
260	        table["error_mw"].abs() / table["actual_load_mw"].abs() * 100.0
261	    )
262	    table.index.name = TIMESTAMP_COLUMN
263	    return table

38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class ModelRun:
40	    training_start: pd.Timestamp
41	    training_end: pd.Timestamp
42	    forecast: pd.Series

47	    year: int

53	def make_target_index() -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
54	    return pd.date_range(TARGET_START, TARGET_END, freq="h", inclusive="left")

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load

80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features
144	
145	
146	def build_model() -> lgb.LGBMRegressor:
147	    return lgb.LGBMRegressor(
148	        objective="regression_l2",
149	        n_estimators=400,
150	        learning_rate=0.04,
151	        num_leaves=16,
152	        max_depth=6,
153	        min_child_samples=50,
154	        subsample=0.9,
155	        subsample_freq=1,
156	        colsample_bytree=0.9,
157	        reg_lambda=1.0,
158	        random_state=RANDOM_SEED,
159	        n_jobs=-1,
160	        verbosity=-1,
161	    )

164	def fit_and_forecast(
165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]

172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:

175	    training_features = build_calendar_features(training.index)
176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180	
181	    forecast = pd.Series(forecast_values, index=forecast_index, name="forecast_load_mw")
182	    return ModelRun(
183	        training_start=training.index[0],
184	        training_end=training.index[-1],
185	        forecast=forecast,

193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)

200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):

207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }
217	
218	
219	def run_backtests(load: pd.Series) -> list[BacktestReport]:
220	    reports: list[BacktestReport] = []
221	    for year in BACKTEST_YEARS:
222	        start = pd.Timestamp(f"{year}-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
223	        forecast_index = pd.date_range(start, periods=TARGET_HOURS, freq="h")
224	        if forecast_index[-1] not in load.index:
225	            continue
226	
227	        run = fit_and_forecast(load, forecast_index)
228	        actual = load.loc[forecast_index]
229	        reports.append(
230	            BacktestReport(
231	                year=year,
232	                training_start_utc=run.training_start.isoformat(),
233	                training_end_utc=run.training_end.isoformat(),
234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports

240	def average_backtest_metrics(backtests: list[BacktestReport]) -> dict[str, float]:
241	    if not backtests:
242	        return {}
243	
244	    metric_names = tuple(backtests[0].metrics)
245	    return {
246	        name: float(np.mean([report.metrics[name] for report in backtests]))
247	        for name in metric_names
248	    }

259	    table["absolute_percentage_error"] = (
260	        table["error_mw"].abs() / table["actual_load_mw"].abs() * 100.0
261	    )
262	    table.index.name = TIMESTAMP_COLUMN
263	    return table

440	    print(f"Training window: {run.training_start.isoformat()} to {run.training_end.isoformat()}")
441	    print(f"Hours forecast: {TARGET_HOURS}")
442	    print(f"MAE:  {metrics['mae_mw']:,.1f} MW")
443	    print(f"RMSE: {metrics['rmse_mw']:,.1f} MW")
444	    print(f"MAPE: {metrics['mape_percent']:.3f}%")

458	def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
459	    default_directory = Path(__file__).resolve().parent

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import argparse
4	import json
5	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
6	from pathlib import Path
7	from typing import Sequence
8	
9	import holidays
10	import lightgbm as lgb
11	import matplotlib.dates as mdates
12	import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
13	import numpy as np
14	import pandas as pd  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
15	from matplotlib.axes import Axes
16	from matplotlib.figure import Figure
17	from numpy.typing import NDArray
18	
19	TIMESTAMP_COLUMN = "utc_timestamp"
20	LOAD_COLUMN = "DE_load_actual_entsoe_transparency"
21	TARGET_START = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
22	TARGET_END = pd.Timestamp("2020-01-08 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
23	TARGET_HOURS = 168
24	TRAINING_YEARS = 2
25	BACKTEST_YEARS = (2017, 2018, 2019)
26	RANDOM_SEED = 42
27	REFERENCE_TIME = pd.Timestamp("2015-01-01 00:00:00", tz="UTC")
28	
29	ACTUAL_COLOR = "#2a78d6"
30	FORECAST_COLOR = "#eb6834"
31	SURFACE_COLOR = "#fcfcfb"
32	TEXT_COLOR = "#0b0b0b"
33	SECONDARY_TEXT_COLOR = "#52514e"
34	MUTED_COLOR = "#898781"
35	GRID_COLOR = "#e1e0d9"
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class ModelRun:
40	    training_start: pd.Timestamp
41	    training_end: pd.Timestamp
42	    forecast: pd.Series
43	
44	
45	@dataclass(frozen=True)
46	class BacktestReport:
47	    year: int
48	    training_start_utc: str
49	    training_end_utc: str
50	    metrics: dict[str, float]
51	
52	
53	def make_target_index() -> pd.DatetimeIndex:
54	    return pd.date_range(TARGET_START, TARGET_END, freq="h", inclusive="left")
55	
56	
57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load
78	
79	
80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")
95	
96	
97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
135	
136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]
137	    features["is_new_year"] = ((local_index.month == 1) & (local_index.day == 1)).astype(int)
138	    features["is_christmas_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 24)).astype(int)
139	    features["is_christmas"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & local_index.day.isin([25, 26])).astype(
140	        int
141	    )
142	    features["is_new_year_eve"] = ((local_index.month == 12) & (local_index.day == 31)).astype(int)
143	    return features

165	    load: pd.Series,
166	    forecast_index: pd.DatetimeIndex,
167	    training_years: int = TRAINING_YEARS,
168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]
170	    training_start = forecast_start - pd.DateOffset(years=training_years)
171	    training = load.loc[(load.index >= training_start) & (load.index < forecast_start)]
172	    if len(training) < 365 * 24:

174

176	    forecast_features = build_calendar_features(forecast_index)
177	    model = build_model()
178	    model.fit(training_features, training.to_numpy(dtype=float))
179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

168	) -> ModelRun:
169	    forecast_start = forecast_index[0]

179	    forecast_values = model.predict(forecast_features)
180

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

228	        actual = load.loc[forecast_index]
229	        reports.append(

232	                training_start_utc=run.training_start.isoformat(),
233	                training_end_utc=run.training_end.isoformat(),
234	                metrics=calculate_metrics(actual.to_numpy(), run.forecast.to_numpy()),
235	            )
236	        )
237	    return reports

189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load
78	
79	
80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual

110	def build_calendar_features(index: pd.DatetimeIndex) -> pd.DataFrame:
111	    if index.tz is None:
112	        raise ValueError("Feature timestamps must be timezone-aware.")
113	
114	    utc_index = index.tz_convert("UTC")
115	    local_index = utc_index.tz_convert("Europe/Berlin")
116	    local_dates = pd.Index(local_index.date)
117	    holiday_calendar = holidays.country_holidays(
118	        "DE", years=range(int(local_index.year.min()) - 1, int(local_index.year.max()) + 2)
119	    )
120	
121	    features = pd.DataFrame(index=utc_index)
122	    features["elapsed_days"] = (utc_index - REFERENCE_TIME).total_seconds() / 86_400.0
123	    features["local_hour"] = local_index.hour
124	    features["weekday"] = local_index.dayofweek
125	    features["day_of_year"] = local_index.dayofyear
126	    features["month"] = local_index.month
127	    features["day_of_month"] = local_index.day
128	
129	    features["hour_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
130	    features["hour_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.hour / 24.0)
131	    features["weekday_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
132	    features["weekday_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofweek / 7.0)
133	    features["year_sin"] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)
134	    features["year_cos"] = np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * local_index.dayofyear / 365.25)

136	    features["is_holiday"] = [int(date in holiday_calendar) for date in local_dates]

- The function is publicly named and has no docstring or documented precondition delegating validation to callers. 189	def calculate_metrics(
190	    actual: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
191	    forecast: Sequence[float] | NDArray[np.float64],
192	) -> dict[str, float]:
193	    actual_array = np.asarray(actual, dtype=float)
194	    forecast_array = np.asarray(forecast, dtype=float)
195	    if actual_array.shape != forecast_array.shape:
196	        raise ValueError("Actual and forecast arrays must have the same shape.")
197	    if actual_array.size == 0:
198	        raise ValueError("Metrics require at least one observation.")
199	    if not np.isfinite(actual_array).all() or not np.isfinite(forecast_array).all():
200	        raise ValueError("Metrics require finite values.")
201	    if np.any(actual_array == 0.0):
202	        raise ValueError("MAPE is undefined when an actual value is zero.")
203	
204	    errors = forecast_array - actual_array
205	    absolute_errors = np.abs(errors)
206	    squared_errors = errors**2
207	    denominator = np.abs(actual_array) + np.abs(forecast_array)
208	    total_variation = np.sum((actual_array - actual_array.mean()) ** 2)
209	
210	    return {
211	        "mae_mw": float(absolute_errors.mean()),
212	        "rmse_mw": float(np.sqrt(squared_errors.mean())),
213	        "mape_percent": float(np.mean(absolute_errors / np.abs(actual_array)) * 100.0),
214	        "smape_percent": float(np.mean(2.0 * absolute_errors / denominator) * 100.0),
215	        "r_squared": float(1.0 - np.sum(squared_errors) / total_variation),
216	    }

57	def load_hourly_load(path: Path) -> pd.Series:
58	    frame = pd.read_csv(path, parse_dates=[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
59	    required_columns = {TIMESTAMP_COLUMN, LOAD_COLUMN}
60	    missing_columns = required_columns.difference(frame.columns)
61	    if missing_columns:
62	        missing = ", ".join(sorted(missing_columns))
63	        raise ValueError(f"Missing required columns: {missing}")
64	
65	    timestamps = pd.DatetimeIndex(frame[TIMESTAMP_COLUMN])
66	    if timestamps.tz is None:
67	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_localize("UTC")
68	    else:
69	        timestamps = timestamps.tz_convert("UTC")
70	
71	    load = pd.Series(
72	        pd.to_numeric(frame[LOAD_COLUMN], errors="raise").to_numpy(dtype=float),
73	        index=timestamps,
74	        name="load_mw",
75	    ).sort_index()
76	    validate_hourly_load(load)
77	    return load

80	def validate_hourly_load(load: pd.Series) -> None:
81	    if load.empty:
82	        raise ValueError("The load series is empty.")
83	    if load.index.has_duplicates:
84	        raise ValueError("The load series contains duplicate timestamps.")
85	    if load.isna().any():
86	        raise ValueError("The load series contains missing values.")
87	    if not np.isfinite(load.to_numpy(dtype=float)).all():
88	        raise ValueError("The load series contains non-finite values.")
89	    if not load.index.is_monotonic_increasing:
90	        raise ValueError("The load timestamps are not sorted.")
91	
92	    expected = pd.date_range(load.index[0], load.index[-1], freq="h")
93	    if not load.index.equals(expected):
94	        raise ValueError("The load series is not continuous at hourly frequency.")

97	def split_training_and_target(load: pd.Series) -> tuple[pd.Series, pd.Series]:
98	    target_index = make_target_index()
99	    missing_target_hours = target_index.difference(load.index)
100	    if not missing_target_hours.empty:
101	        raise ValueError(f"The dataset is missing {len(missing_target_hours)} target hours.")
102	
103	    training = load.loc[load.index < TARGET_START]
104	    actual = load.loc[target_index]
105	    if training.empty:
106	        raise ValueError("No observations are available before the forecast period.")
107	    return training, actual
